segments.html:
// Declare Viewer — a live, syntax-highlighted view of a Declare source file.
//
// It renders nothing on its own: the server runs the compiler's highlighter
// over a `.declare` file and hands the resulting segments to this app through
// the host→app seed channel (app.demoSources), so the Viewer is a plain
// consumer. Each segment is either prose — the Markdown carried in a block
// comment, rendered by the Markdown class — or code — a run of
// syntax-highlighted <pre> HTML whose per-token <span> classes this app's
// `textStyles` map colors (theme-aware, so the same segments render light or
// dark).
//
// Reach it with a request type: a bare `foo.declare?viewer` opens the default
// Reader tab (the program URL is the address — a directory carries no
// behavior). The Reader / Source / Edit triple (?viewer=reader | source | edit)
// switches between the rendered view, the verbatim source, and an editing
// workbench (the source in an editor, the running program below it, compile
// errors sandwiched between); the A stepper zooms every text size; the
// sun / half-disc / moon switch picks Light / System / Dark.
//
// The code is linked: an `include [ "…" ]` path opens that file; a class the
// program declares opens where it is declared, at that line; a platform class
// opens its reference page. The reader follows a file link in place (the
// location names the file, and the host's Back walks it), and an include's
// Edit tab — classes, no App, nothing to run — says which program to edit
// instead.

include [ "reference.declare" ]

// the appearance switch names its icons in data, so the build keeps the classes

// one segment: prose (Markdown) or code (colored, monospace <pre>). Exactly one
// child is visible, so the segment's auto-height is that child's height. Prose is
// inset (a narrower reading column); code spans the full width, so the two read as
// distinct — commentary vs. program — and code gets the room.

class Block [ kind: string = "",
    md: string = "",
    html: string = "",
    lines: number = 1,                           // the code's line count, for its declarations' markers
    nested: boolean = false,                     // born inside a declaration's body: an aside, not a section break
    joinBelow: boolean = false,                  // the next segment is a nested aside: this card's bottom-left squares

    width = 100%,

    // prose reads like a book: left-aligned to the shared spine, capped at the
    // reading measure, with space above it that becomes the section break.
    // A nested aside — a block comment inside a class or instance body — keeps
    // the code's teal spine running through it and sits inset to the code's own
    // text gutter, so the declaration it interrupts still reads as one
    // specimen: header card, threaded aside, body card.

    prose: Markdown [ visible = { classroot.kind == "prose" }, x = { classroot.nested ? 20 : 0 },
        y = { classroot.nested ? 8 : app.proseTopPad },
        width = { Math.min(parent.width - (classroot.nested ? 20 : 0), app.proseMeasure * app.fontScale) },
        text = { classroot.md }, fontScale = { app.fontScale }, lineHeight = 1.6,
        bodyColor = { provided("theme").text }, selectable = true ],

    // the thread: the code spine, continued through the aside — unbroken and at
    // the spine's own weight. It reaches up across the column's 12px gap to
    // meet the card above, and runs a hair past the prose so a resuming code
    // card's bridge (below) meets it across the next gap.

    thread: View [ visible = { classroot.kind == "prose" && classroot.nested }, x = 0, y = -12, width = 2,
        height = { classroot.prose.y + classroot.prose.height + 20 },
        fill = { provided("theme").accentSecondary } ],

    // a resuming code card's half of the same continuity: cover the gap above
    // it so its interior spine connects to the aside's thread

    bridge: View [ visible = { classroot.kind == "code" && classroot.nested }, x = 0, y = -12, width = 2,
        height = 12, fill = { provided("theme").accentSecondary } ],

    // code is the specimen: borderless, on a quiet tint, bonded to the comment
    // above it, running the full width with a teal spine on the shared left edge.
    // The <pre> never wraps — long constraint lines scroll horizontally.

    code: View [ visible = { classroot.kind == "code" }, width = 100%,
        height = { this.body.height + 32 },
        clip = true,                             // the card contains its code: long lines clip at the box (the DOM's pre scrolls natively; the sealed surface must say so)

        // the card's text gutter is the card's own content box. The spine is
        // the card's own left border, not a child, so nothing here has to opt
        // out of the inset.

        padding = [16, 20, 16, 20],

        // the card's own shape, stated exactly: rounded everywhere except the
        // corner an aside joins — the card above an aside squares its
        // bottom-left, the card below its top-left. Per-corner radii say it
        // directly, and the spine is the left side of the stroke, following the
        // same arcs, so the thread meets the gap connectors dead-on.

        fill = { provided("theme").codeBg },
        cornerRadius = { [classroot.nested ? 0 : 8, 8, 8, classroot.joinBelow ? 0 : 8] },
        stroke = { [null, null, null, stroke(2, provided("theme").accentSecondary)] },
        body: View [ width = 100%, scrolls = x, height = { this.contentHeight },
            HTMLText [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 100%,
                html = { classroot.html }, fontScale = { app.fontScale },
                textStyles = { app.codeTextStyles() }, bodyColor = { app.codeFg() }, selectable = true,

                // file links read as links: the conventional blue, underlined

                linkColor = { app.isDark ? 0x58A6FF : 0x0969DA }, linkUnderline = true ]
            ],

        // the declarations this card holds: a marker at each one's line, named
        // for it, so a link to `@Name` lands there — the platform's reveal waits
        // for the file, then scrolls the marker to the top. A marker is shown
        // only once its card's code has a height (the browser measures it a
        // frame after it renders), and the reveal does not land on what is not
        // shown. Named only while the reader shows, so the source view's
        // markers can take the same names.

        View [ datapath = :marks[], width = 1, height = 1,
            anchor = { app.mode == "reader" ? :name : "" },
            visible = { parent.body.height > 0 },
            y = { :line * parent.body.height / Math.max(1, classroot.lines) } ]
        ]
    ]


// small / reset / large "A" — steps the reader font zoom (docs' SizeBtn).

class SizeBtn extends Control [ width = 34, height = 30, cornerRadius = 6,

    glyph: number = 14,
    delta: number = 0,
    fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").controlHovered : null },
    press() { app.fontScale = classroot.delta == 0 ? 0.9
        : Math.max(0.7, Math.min(1.6, Math.round((app.fontScale + classroot.delta) * 100) / 100)) },

    lbl: TextLabel [ fontWeight = semibold, fontSize = { classroot.glyph }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
        text = "A", wrap = false, x = center ]
    ]


App [ fill = { provided("theme").background },

    // a declaration a link lands on sits a little below the top of the page

    revealInset = 24,

    // the page title is the viewed file itself ("calendar.declare") — the seeds
    // land after boot, so the served title stands until the path arrives

    appName = { app.baseName() },

    // Embedded self-loading: a host (the desktop) passes `env.program` — a
    // program path valid in the host's transport base — and this app fetches
    // its own reader artifacts from that program URL's ?segments and ?file
    // requests: the same bytes the serve wrapper seeds via demoSources,
    // pulled by the app itself, on either hosting mode. A seeded
    // demoSources still wins wherever both exist.
    //
    // Following an include is the same self-loading, aimed elsewhere: the
    // location names a file by its served path (`reader/apps/weather/
    // weather-art.declare` — the address bar's own spelling, minus the leading
    // slash, so the fragment is honest shareable coordinates), and these two
    // sources fetch it — the seeds keep serving only the file the page was
    // opened on.

    segSrc: DataSource [ format = "text", auto = true, url = { app.srcUrl("?segments") },
        // the program's class index comes with the file it was opened on, and
        // stays while the reader follows links to other files

        onLoad() { if (app.fileRel == "") app.openedDefs = app.defsOf(this.value) }
        ],

    // when the raw file lands (the env-driven embedded case has no seeds),
    // publish it on the live channel: the edit pane's island then runs the
    // viewed program as soon as the tab opens — no first keystroke needed

    rawSrc: DataSource [ format = "text", auto = true, url = { app.srcUrl("?file") },
        onLoad() { if (app.liveCard == "" && app.fileRel == "") { app.liveCard = "__raw__"; app.liveSource = "" + (this.value || "") } }
        ],

    // the url the two sources fetch: the followed file when the location names
    // one, else the host's program when embedded, nothing when the seeds serve.
    // With a host's program, a followed file is spelled the way the program
    // is — relative to the same base, or a whole URL — so it is fetched as
    // written. Standalone, it is named by its path from the deploy root, and
    // the sources resolve against the opened program's own directory, so the
    // path climbs from there to the root: the same request on a host serving
    // at its origin and on one serving under a subpath (a project's GitHub
    // Pages).

    srcUrl(q: string) -> string {
        if (app.fileRel == "") return app.hostProgram == "" ? "" : app.hostProgram + q
        if (app.hostProgram != "") return app.fileRel + q
        const depth = app.seededPath().replace(/^\/+/, "").split("/").length - 1
        return "../".repeat(depth) + app.fileRel + q
        },

    // the program a host names as the subject (the desktop's viewer window); "" standalone

    hostProgram: string = { hostProvided("subject", "") },

    // where the docs app is, for a platform class's reference page — "" on a
    // host that has none (the Mac app provides "")

    docsBase: string = { hostProvided("docs", "apps/docs/") },

    barH: number = 52,
    topM: number = 40,    // reader top margin (foot matches it at the bottom)
    headH: number = { 46 * app.fontScale },    // filename title + rule, above the body

    // "reader" = highlighted + Markdown, "source" = verbatim, "edit" = live
    // workbench — the viewer's location. The `?viewer=` request seeds the
    // opening tab (the host translates the query into the initial location);
    // a tab click writes `app.location` and this derives back from it, so the
    // tab is a single source of truth that back/forward walk for free.

    // The location's grammar: `<mode>` alone views the file the page was
    // opened on; `<mode>/<served path>` views another — an include or a
    // library file the reader followed, named exactly as the host serves it
    // (`reader/apps/weather/weather-art.declare`). One spelling for every
    // file, and the fragment names the file to anyone it is handed to.

    // A trailing `@Name` lands on a declaration in that file (`reader/apps/
    // asteroids/game.declare@Game`); `place` is the location without it.

    place: string = { (app.location || "").split("@")[0] },
    mode: string = { (app.place || "reader").split("/")[0] || "reader" },
    fileRel: string = { app.place.indexOf("/") < 0 ? "" : app.place.slice(app.place.indexOf("/") + 1) },

    // The history walk is the host's — the browser's Back/Forward, the mac
    // titlebar's ‹ › — because a followed file is one location entry and a tab
    // switch replaces its entry (the Segmented's `replace`), so Back walks
    // files, never tabs. The viewer draws no chrome of its own for it.

    fontScale: number = 0.9,    // reader font zoom (0.9 = the comfortable default; the A stepper drives it)
    proseMeasure: number = 560,    // prose reading measure (matches the docs); code runs wider off the same left edge
    proseTopPad: number = 22,    // space above a prose block — reads as the section break
    themeMode: string = "auto",
    liveCard: string = "",      // the edit tab republishes each keystroke on this pair …
    liveSource: string = "",    // … and the host recompiles it, feeding app.liveReport back

    // auto follows the HOST's appearance when a host provides one, else the
    // system preference. The bar's AppearanceSwitch sets "light" or "dark",
    // and from then on that holds.

    isDark: boolean = { app.themeMode == "auto"
        ? hostProvided("dark", app.dark)
        : app.themeMode == "dark" },

    // The house preset, plus this app's two domain names — and no private
    // values for the standard tokens, so the same markdown reads one color
    // here and in the desktop's reader window. A reader's page is a sheet, so
    // it paints `surface` — the token the desktop's window paints — and the
    // chrome around it recedes to `background`.

    theme = { { ...(app.isDark ? SanFranciscoDark : SanFrancisco), ...app.domainTheme() } },

    // The highlight() segments, seeded by the server as a JSON string on the
    // host→app channel; parse + normalise so every record has kind/md/html.

    doc: Dataset [ contents = { app.parseDoc() } ],
    plainMarks: Dataset [ contents = { { marks: app.marksIn(app.plainHtml()) } } ],

    parseDoc() {
        const raw = app.fileRel == "" ? ((app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__source__"]) || app.segSrc.value || "[]") : (app.segSrc.value || "[]")
        let segs = []
        // two shapes for one material: the seeded channel is the bare array; the
        // ?segments request wraps it ({ path, segments }) — accept either
        try { const p = JSON.parse(raw); segs = Array.isArray(p) ? p : (p && p.segments) || [] } catch (e) { segs = [] }
        // graceful floor: a host with no highlighter (a static host answers no
        // ?segments) still reads — the raw file as one code block. It waits for
        // segSrc to SETTLE (loaded or failed), not merely to be empty: `?file`
        // is a plain passthrough and `?segments` runs highlight() over the same
        // bytes, so on a real host `?file` always lands first, and flooring on
        // "empty so far" would show one plain code block and then replace it
        // with the prose/code segments a moment later. (Standalone, the server
        // seeds __source__ synchronously, so this branch does not run.)
        if (segs.length == 0 && (app.rawSrc.value || "") != ""
            && (app.segSrc.loaded || app.segSrc.failed)) {
            const e = ("" + app.rawSrc.value).replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">")
            segs = [({ kind: "code", html: "<pre>" + e + "</pre>" })]
            }
        return ({ segments: segs.map((s, i) => ({ kind: s.kind, md: s.md || "", html: s.kind == "code" ? app.linkFiles(s.html || "") : "", nested: s.nested == true,
            joinBelow: segs[i + 1] != null && segs[i + 1].nested == true,
            lines: s.kind == "code" ? app.lineCount(s.html || "") : 1, marks: s.kind == "code" ? app.marksIn(s.html || "") : [] })) })
        },

    // a code block's lines, and the classes and schemas declared on them —
    // read off the html with its tags taken out (the highlighter keeps the text
    // verbatim inside its spans)

    lineCount(html: string) -> number { return html.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "").split("\n").length },
    marksIn(html: string) -> object[] {
        const out = []
        const lines = html.replace(/<[^>]*>/g, "").split("\n")
        for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
            const m = /^\s*(class|schema)\s+([A-Z]\w*)/.exec(lines[i])
            if (m != null) out.push({ name: m[2], line: i })
            }
        return out
        },

    // LINKS in code. A code segment's html is the highlighter's <pre> of
    // <span class=…> tokens, and three shapes become links — each an <a href>
    // the reader follows through app.follow, so it works on every renderer and
    // the history walks it:
    //   (1) a path inside an `include [ … ]` or `script [ … ]` directive — that
    //       file, resolved against the viewed file's folder;
    //   (2) a class or schema the program declares (`Game [`, `extends Game`,
    //       `: Task`) — where it is declared, at that line (`@Game`);
    //   (3) a platform class (`Button [`) — its reference page, where the host
    //       has the docs (`docsBase`).
    // A name at its own declaration (`class Game`) is not a link.

    linkFiles(html: string) -> string {
        const dir = app.viewedDir()
        const base = app.mode
        const q = String.fromCharCode(34)                     // the double quote, kept out of this body's regexes
        const inc = new RegExp('<span class=' + q + 'k' + q + '>(include|script)<\\/span>\\s*\\[([\\s\\S]*?)\\]', 'g')
        const str = new RegExp('<span class=' + q + 's' + q + '>' + q + '([^' + q + ']+)' + q + '<\\/span>', 'g')
        const tag = new RegExp('(<span class=' + q + 'k' + q + '>class<\\/span> |schema )?<span class=' + q + 't' + q + '>([A-Z]\\w*)<\\/span>', 'g')
        // the anchor's text is bare (no accent span inside): the accent would
        // compose over the link color, and a link should read as a link —
        // linkColor + linkUnderline on the HTMLText style it. The quote marks
        // stay outside the anchor, in the string accent: the file is the link,
        // its quoting is syntax.
        const quote = '<span class=' + q + 's' + q + '>' + q + '</span>'
        const out = html.replace(inc, (m, kw, body) =>
            '<span class=' + q + 'k' + q + '>' + kw + '</span> [' + body.replace(str, (m2, p) =>
                quote + '<a href=' + q + '#' + base + '/' + app.resolveRel(dir, p) + q + '>' + p + '</a>' + quote) + ']')
        return out.replace(tag, (m, decl, t) => {
            if (decl) return m
            const at = app.declaredAt(t)
            if (at != "") return '<a href=' + q + '#' + at + q + '>' + t + '</a>'
            if (app.docsBase != "" && REFERENCE_CLASSES.includes(t)) return '<a href=' + q + app.docsBase + '#reference/' + t + q + '>' + t + '</a>'
            return m
            })
        },

    // THE CLASS INDEX — name → the declaring file's path from a file's folder
    // ("" for that file itself), worked out by the host (the compiler's
    // programIndex) and handed over with the file: seeded as __defs__, or in
    // the ?segments payload. The program's index comes with the file the page
    // opened on; a followed file brings its own declarations.

    openedDefs: Record<string, string> = { {} },
    defsOf(payload: string) -> Record<string, string> {
        try { const p = JSON.parse(payload || "null"); return (p && p.defs) || {} } catch (e) { return {} }
        },
    programDefs() -> Record<string, string> {
        try { const s = app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__defs__"]; if (s) return JSON.parse(s) } catch (e) { }
        return app.openedDefs
        },
    openingDir() -> string { const p = app.seededPath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? "" : p.slice(0, i + 1) },

    // where `t` is declared, as a location in the current tab — "" when the
    // program declares no such name. The file shown now answers first.

    declaredAt(t: string) -> string {
        const here = app.fileRel == "" ? app.programDefs() : app.defsOf(app.segSrc.value || "")
        if (here[t] === "") return app.mode + (app.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + app.fileRel) + "@" + t
        const p = app.programDefs()[t]
        if (typeof p != "string") return ""
        return app.mode + (p == "" ? "" : "/" + app.resolveRel(app.openingDir(), p)) + "@" + t
        },

    // a path relative to `dir`, normalised: `rooms/../art.declare` → `art.declare`.
    // A climb past the start is kept (`../calendar/` + `x.declare` →
    // `../calendar/x.declare`: the host's program may sit beside this one), and
    // a whole URL resolves as a URL (`file:///…/apps/sampler/`).

    resolveRel(dir: string, p: string) -> string {
        if (/^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:\/\//i.test(dir)) return new URL(p, dir).href
        const parts = (dir + p).split("/")
        const stack: string[] = []
        for (const s of parts) {
            if (s == "..") { if (stack.length == 0 || stack[stack.length - 1] == "..") stack.push(s); else stack.pop() }
            else if (s != "." && s != "") stack.push(s)
            }
        return stack.join("/")
        },

    // the verbatim file as one escaped, monospace <pre> — the plain-text view

    plainHtml() {
        const e = app.rawText().replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">")
        return "<pre>" + e + "</pre>"
        },

    // the verbatim text of the viewed file — the seeds' for the opened file,
    // the fetched one for a followed include

    rawText() -> string {
        return app.fileRel == "" ? ((app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__raw__"]) || app.rawSrc.value || "") : ("" + (app.rawSrc.value || ""))
        },

    // an include declares classes and no App — it cannot run on its own, so
    // the Edit tab shows where to edit instead (the program that includes it)

    // (the comment-stripping regex is built from a string: a literal `/*` inside
    // a { } body reads as a block comment to the body scanner)

    hasApp(src: string) -> boolean { return src != "" && /^\s*App\s*\[/m.test(src.replace(new RegExp('\\/\\*[\\s\\S]*?\\*\\/', 'g'), "")) },
    isInclude: boolean = { app.rawText() != "" && !app.hasApp(app.rawText()) },

    // is the file this page opened on a runnable program? False when the page
    // was opened directly on an include — then there is no program to point at.

    seededRunnable: boolean = { app.hasApp((app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__raw__"]) || (app.fileRel == "" ? app.rawText() : "")) },

    // the file's tree-relative path, split so the header can bold the filename:
    // the opened program's, or the followed file's resolved against it

    seededPath() -> string { return (app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__path__"]) || (app.hostProgram != "" ? app.hostProgram : "source") },

    // the viewed file's served path: the followed file's own, else the opened program's

    filePath() { return app.fileRel == "" ? app.seededPath() : app.fileRel },

    // the viewed file's directory (served), the base an include path in it resolves against

    viewedDir() -> string { const p = app.filePath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? "" : p.slice(0, i + 1) },

    // the compiler's line count, as the host hands it over (programMetrics():
    // total / code / comment / blank, and `app` — the same plus `files` — when
    // the file declares the App: the file and everything it includes, the
    // library's left out). Seeded as __metrics__, or carried by the ?segments
    // payload when the viewer loads the file itself. Lines are counted with
    // their comments and without; blank lines are neither.

    metrics() {
        let m = null
        if (app.fileRel == "") { try { m = JSON.parse((app.demoSources && app.demoSources["__metrics__"]) || "null") } catch (e) { m = null } }
        if (m == null && app.segSrc.value) {
            try { const p = JSON.parse(app.segSrc.value); m = (p && p.metrics) || null } catch (e) { m = null }
            }
        return m
        },
    counts(c: { code: number; comment: number }) -> string {
        return (c.code + c.comment).toLocaleString("en-US") + " lines with comments, " + c.code.toLocaleString("en-US") + " without"
        },
    hasMetrics: boolean = { app.metrics() != null },
    hasWhole: boolean = { app.hasMetrics && app.metrics().app != null && app.metrics().app.files > 1 },
    fileCounts: string = { app.hasMetrics ? app.counts(app.metrics()) + (app.hasWhole ? " ·" : "") : "" },
    appCounts: string = { app.hasWhole ? "(" + app.metrics().app.files + " files): " + app.counts(app.metrics().app) : "" },
    dirName() { const p = app.filePath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? "" : p.slice(0, i + 1) },
    baseName() { const p = app.filePath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? p : p.slice(i + 1) },

    // the editor foreground (plain text / punctuation) behind the accent spans

    codeFg() { return app.isDark ? 0xABB2BF : 0x24292F },

    // role → color, theme-aware. Keys match the <span class> names highlight()
    // emits: k t a s n h p o b c. Dark = One Dark; light = a cool, light-native
    // set (gold-on-white reads as a dark-mode leftover, so types go purple/blue).

    codeTextStyles() {
        const c = app.isDark
            ? ({ k: 0xC678DD, t: 0xE5C07B, a: 0xE06C75, s: 0x98C379, n: 0xD19A66, h: 0x56B6C2, p: 0x61AFEF, o: 0x56B6C2, b: 0x9DA5B4, c: 0x6A737D })
            : ({ k: 0xCF222E, t: 0x8250DF, a: 0xB5452B, s: 0x1A7F37, n: 0x9A6700, h: 0x0E7490, p: 0x0550AE, o: 0xCF222E, b: 0x6B7280, c: 0x8A919C })
        return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(c).map(([k, v]) => [k, { textColor: v }]))
        },

    // What this app adds to the house palette, and nothing more.
    //
    // `codeBg` is the house backdrop showing through the page — a code well is
    // recessed, which is the same relationship in both modes and needs no value
    // of its own. `accentSecondary` is the far end of the brand gradient (the
    // wordmark, a card's spine, the live grip); the house has one accent, and a
    // second hue is this app's, not the platform's.

    domainTheme() {
        return ({ codeBg: (app.isDark ? SanFranciscoDark : SanFrancisco).background,
            accentSecondary: app.isDark ? 0x37E0C8 : 0x12A594 })
        },

    // scrolling reader; the column fills the window between fixed 48px gutters, so
    // code grows with the window while prose stays capped at its reading measure.
    // `foot` sits just below the active view for a bottom margin matching `topM`.

    content: View [ x = 0, y = { app.barH }, width = { app.hostWidth }, height = { app.hostHeight - app.barH },
        visible = { app.mode != "edit" },
        scrolls = y, selectable = true, fill = { provided("theme").surface },

        // the filename as a page title — the directory muted, the file bold — with
        // a rule under it; the body starts below (headH)

        head: View [ y = { app.topM }, width = { app.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            title: View [ layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
                d: Text [ fontSize = { 21 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted }, text = { app.dirName() } ],
                n: Text [ fontSize = { 21 * app.fontScale }, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = { app.baseName() } ],

                // the size of the thing, quietly: the compiler's own count

                gapm: View [ width = 14, height = 1 ],
                m: View [ y = { 8 * app.fontScale }, visible = { app.hasMetrics },
                    fontSize = { 13 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
                    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 4 ],
                    Text [ fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, text = "This file:" ],
                    Text [ wrap = false, text = { app.fileCounts } ],
                    Text [ fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, visible = { app.hasWhole }, text = "Whole app" ],
                    Text [ wrap = false, visible = { app.hasWhole }, text = { app.appCounts } ]
                    ]
                ],

            // a blue→teal thread of the brand accent, the origin of the code spine

            rule: View [ y = { 34 * app.fontScale }, width = 100%, height = 2, cornerRadius = 1,
                opacity = { app.isDark ? 0.72 : 1 },
                fill = { gradient("90deg", provided("theme").accent, provided("theme").accentSecondary) } ]
            ],

        // highlighted view: prose + colored code segments

        col: View [ visible = { app.mode == "reader" }, y = { app.topM + app.headH }, width = { app.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            datapath = { app.doc.value },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 12 ],
            Block [ datapath = :segments[], kind = :kind, md = :md, html = :html, nested = { :nested == true }, joinBelow = { :joinBelow == true }, lines = { :lines } ]
            ],

        // plain view: the verbatim source as one monospace flow (same size/theme)

        plain: View [ visible = { app.mode == "source" }, y = { app.topM + app.headH }, width = { app.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            fill = { provided("theme").codeBg }, cornerRadius = 8, clip = true,
            height = { this.body.height + 32 },
            spine: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 2, height = 100%, fill = { provided("theme").accentSecondary } ],

            // verbatim source at the house code rendition — the same face and size
            // as the reader's highlighted code, so the two views read identically.

            body: View [ x = 20, y = 16, width = { parent.width - 40 }, scrolls = x, height = { this.contentHeight },
                HTMLText [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 100%, html = { app.plainHtml() },
                    fontScale = { app.fontScale }, bodyColor = { app.codeFg() }, selectable = true ]
                ],

            // the declarations' markers, as on the reader's cards — named only
            // while this view shows

            marks: View [ y = 16, width = 1, height = 1, datapath = { app.plainMarks.value },
                View [ datapath = :marks[], width = 1, height = 1,
                    anchor = { app.mode == "source" ? :name : "" },
                    visible = { parent.parent.body.height > 0 },
                    y = { :line * parent.parent.body.height / Math.max(1, app.lineCount(app.plainHtml())) } ]
                ]
            ],

        // bottom margin: a spacer just past the active view's bottom edge

        foot: View [ width = 8, height = 48,
            y = { app.topM + app.headH + (app.mode == "reader" ? parent.col.height : parent.plain.height) } ]
        ],

    // Live-edit workbench — a fixed stack filling the window below the bar: the
    // source in an editor on top, the running program below, compile errors
    // sandwiched between. The pieces are the host's generic live loop: the island
    // is named "run:__raw__" (its seed IS the viewed file), the editor publishes
    // every keystroke on liveCard/liveSource, and app.liveReport carries the last
    // recompile's rendered report ("" = clean; the island keeps the last good
    // render while it shows). A file with no App declaration reports instead of
    // running — honest, if unglamorous.

    // An include on the Edit tab: it declares classes and no App, so there
    // is nothing to run — one centered line points at the one program this
    // page actually knows, the one it opened on. (Which programs include a
    // file is unknowable in general — any program may — so the message claims
    // nothing about inclusion.)

    noRun: View [ visible = { app.mode == "edit" && app.isInclude }, x = 0, y = { app.barH },
        width = { app.hostWidth }, height = { app.hostHeight - app.barH }, fill = { provided("theme").surface },

        // two centered lines with a blank line between; the second names the
        // page's own program when it has one, and claims nothing otherwise

        l1: Text [ x = center, y = { parent.height / 2 - 44 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false,
            fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
            text = "This file declares classes — there is no App to run." ],

        row: View [ visible = { app.seededRunnable }, x = center, y = { parent.l1.y + 44 * app.fontScale },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
            Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted }, text = "Edit " ],
            name: Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, fontWeight = semibold,
                textColor = { app.isDark ? 0x58A6FF : 0x0969DA },

                // a location write, not a `link` attr: "edit" is the viewer's own
                // location grammar, not a `shows` destination — the registry
                // (rightly) refuses the literal form, and the write is the same
                // edge the tabs emit

                text = { app.seededPath().split("/").pop() || "" },
                onClick() { app.location = "edit" }
                ],
            Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted }, text = ", the program this page opened on." ]
            ],

        alt: Text [ visible = { !app.seededRunnable }, x = center, y = { parent.l1.y + 44 * app.fontScale }, wrap = false,
            fontSize = { 15 * app.fontScale }, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
            text = "Open a program that includes it to edit live." ]
        ],

    live: View [ visible = { app.mode == "edit" && !app.isInclude }, x = 0, y = { app.barH },
        width = { app.hostWidth }, height = { app.hostHeight - app.barH },
        fill = { provided("theme").surface },

        // the divider y: 0 = not dragged yet (a 42% default); the grip writes it

        split: number = 0,
        editorH: number = { split > 0 ? split : Math.floor(height * 0.42) },
        edited: boolean = false,    // an edit exists (arms Revert; onInput sets it)

        editor: TextInput [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 100%, height = { parent.editorH },
            multiline = true, spellcheck = false, wrap = false, padding = 14,

            // the A stepper drives every pane, this one included

            fontFamily = ["ui-monospace", "monospace"], fontSize = { 12 * app.fontScale },
            textColor = { app.codeFg() },
            fill = { provided("theme").codeBg },
            initial = { app.demoSources["__raw__"] || app.rawSrc.value || "" },
            onInput() { parent.edited = true; app.liveCard = "__raw__"; app.liveSource = text }
            ],

        // Revert — restores the file's pristine text and recompiles it; armed
        // only once an edit exists, quiet (and inert) until then

        revert: View [ y = 10, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6,
            x = { parent.width - this.width - 14 },
            width = { this.lbl.width + 18 },
            opacity = { parent.edited ? 1 : 0.35 },
            stroke = { stroke(1, provided("theme").line) },
            fill = { hovered && parent.edited ? provided("theme").controlHovered : provided("theme").control },
            onClick() {
                if (!parent.edited) return
                const raw = app.demoSources["__raw__"] || app.rawSrc.value || ""
                parent.editor.text = raw
                parent.edited = false
                app.liveCard = "__raw__"; app.liveSource = raw
                },
            lbl: TextLabel [ fontSize = 11, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false, x = center,
                textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted }, text = "Revert" ]
            ],

        // the divider: the press captures the pointer to this view (the router's
        // capture model — the calendar's drag uses the same), so its move/up fire
        // for the whole drag wherever the pointer goes. The move reads the
        // pointer's app-space y (its own event coords are grip-local and the
        // grip is what's moving); the shield (the last child) merely blocks
        // the browser's native text selection in the editor beneath.

        grip: View [ x = 0, y = { parent.editorH }, width = 100%, height = 6,
            dragging: boolean = false,
            fill = { dragging || hovered ? provided("theme").accentSecondary : provided("theme").line },
            drag(y: number) { parent.split = Math.max(120, Math.min(parent.height - 160, y)) },
            onPointerDown()  { dragging = true },
            onPointerMove()  { if (dragging) drag(app.pointerY - app.barH) },
            onPointerUp()    { dragging = false }
            ],

        // the error sandwich: the last recompile's report in full, only while one
        // stands — wrapped multi-line text, the docs/homepage treatment, so the
        // report reads past its "1 error" summary line

        report: View [ visible = { app.liveReport != "" }, x = 0, y = { parent.editorH + 6 },
            width = 100%, clip = true,
            height = { Math.min(200, this.msg.height + 20) },
            fill = { app.isDark ? 0x2A1517 : 0xFDECEC },
            bar: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 3, height = 100%, fill = { app.isDark ? 0xE0525E : 0xC93B47 } ],
            msg: Text [ x = 14, y = 10, width = { parent.width - 28 }, wrap = true,
                fontFamily = ["ui-monospace", "monospace"], fontSize = 11,
                textColor = { app.isDark ? 0xFF8B8B : 0xB42318 }, text = { app.liveReport } ]
            ],

        // the running program — an embedded child app in a host island, swapped
        // to each clean recompile (renderChild); a floor-declaring app pans here

        run: AppIsland [ x = 0, y = { parent.editorH + 6 + (app.liveReport != "" ? parent.report.height : 0) },
            width = 100%,
            height = { parent.height - this.y },
            program = { app.mode == "edit" ? "__raw__" : "" },
            focusable = true,
            onPointerDown() { Focus.focus(this) }   // a press hands the running program the keyboard
            ],

        // the drag shield — last child, so it sits over everything while a
        // divider drag is on. The router already captures the drag to the grip;
        // this view's whole job is to be the browser's native hit target, so the
        // editor's textarea underneath cannot rubber-band a text selection.

        shield: View [ visible = { parent.grip.dragging }, x = 0, y = 0,
            width = 100%, height = 100% ]
        ],

    // top bar: the brand (left) · Reader / Source / Edit (centre) · type-size
    // stepper + theme (right). The brand is the house rendition — gradient
    // "Declare", solid app name — sized and placed as in Calendar and Docs.

    bar: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { app.hostWidth }, height = { app.barH }, fill = { provided("theme").background },

        hair: View [ x = 0, y = { app.barH - 1 }, width = 100%, height = 1, fill = { provided("theme").line } ],

        brand: View [ x = 20, y = { (app.barH - 22) / 2 }, height = 22,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 5 ],

            // "Declare" is the way home — navigate() resolves against the distro
            // root, so this works on either host at any mount point

            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * fontSize }, wrap = false,
                textFill = { gradient("90deg", provided("theme").accent, provided("theme").accentSecondary) }, text = "Declare",
                onClick() { app.navigate("apps/homepage/homepage.declare") }
                ],
            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * fontSize }, wrap = false,
                textColor = { provided("theme").text }, text = "Viewer" ]
            ],

        // Reader / Source / Edit. The tab writes `app.location`, and `app.mode`
        // derives back from it — so the switch stays a single source of truth
        // that back/forward walk for free. `Segmented` keeps that seam intact:
        // `value` reads the derived mode, `input` writes the location.

        modeSwitch: Segmented [ y = { (app.barH - 30) / 2 }, height = 30, width = 244,
            x = { Math.max(200, (app.hostWidth - 244) / 2) },
            replace = true,        // a tab switch never buries Back — the walk is between files
            value = { app.mode },

            // Keep the viewed file across tabs: a bare `location = v` here would
            // drop the followed include (the choice's own location carries the
            // suffix, but this write runs after it and wins the settle). The
            // keyboard path (Enter on a segment) arrives only here, so this must
            // build the full location itself — and replace, like the click
            // path, so no tab switch ever buries Back.

            input(v: object) { app.follow("#" + ("" + v) + (app.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + app.fileRel), true) },

            // each tab states its location, which is what makes the switch a link
            // the crawler can follow — without it this app emits one document
            // (the default) and Source and Edit are unreachable to extraction

            // …and keeps the viewed file: switching tabs on a followed include
            // stays on that include

            choices = { [ ({ id: "reader", label: "Reader", location: "reader" + (app.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + app.fileRel) }),
                          ({ id: "source", label: "Source", location: "source" + (app.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + app.fileRel) }),
                          ({ id: "edit",   label: "Edit",   location: "edit" + (app.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + app.fileRel) }) ] }
            ],

        size: View [ y = { (app.barH - 30) / 2 }, x = { parent.themeSwitch.x - this.width - 8 }, height = 30,
            width = { this.contentWidth },
            cornerRadius = 8, fill = { provided("theme").surface }, stroke = { stroke(1, provided("theme").line) },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 11, delta = -0.1 ],
            d1: View [ width = 1, height = 18, y = 6, fill = { provided("theme").line } ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 15, delta = 0 ],
            d2: View [ width = 1, height = 18, y = 6, fill = { provided("theme").line } ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 19, delta = 0.1 ]
            ],

        themeSwitch: AppearanceSwitch [ y = { (app.barH - this.height) / 2 }, x = { app.hostWidth - this.width - 16 },
            dark = { app.isDark },
            input(v: boolean) { app.themeMode = v ? "dark" : "light" }
            ]
        ]
    ]
